candidates.name: Data-driven type 2 diabetes subtypes (insulin-deficient vs insulin-resistant clusters)
candidates.measure: HOMA2-B and HOMA2-IR (fasting insulin or C-peptide based), used with age, BMI and HbA1c
candidates.measure_type: fasting-based (HOMA from fasting insulin or C-peptide)
candidates.decision: Assign a subtype to predict complications and choose or intensify glucose-lowering treatment
candidates.evidence: C101 (consensus report) describes k-means clustering on HOMA2-B/HOMA2-IR, replicated in 22 studies, and cautions that individual-level subtype probabilities are often low. C269 (review) says C-peptide HOMA indices are needed to classify novel subgroups. Only excerpts read; no treatment-outcome trial seen in the digest.
candidates.guideline_mention: C101 is an international consensus report that discusses it as a precision-medicine gap; it does not recommend routine use (excerpt-level).
candidates.why_not_covered: Row 17 covers individual risk prediction, monitoring and screening with HOMA-IR/TyG. Subtype assignment to steer therapy is a different decision and uses HOMA2-B as well as HOMA2-IR.
candidates.first_pass_viability: Likely tier D: prognostic clustering is replicated but treatment benefit is unproven and C101 itself flags low individual-level probabilities.
candidates.needed: A randomised or well-designed trial showing that subtype-guided treatment beats standard care, a fixed assay-independent cut-off, and a stable individual-level classifier.

candidates.name: Risk-stratified lifestyle intervention in prediabetes using insulin secretion/sensitivity from a multi-sample OGTT
candidates.patient_group: Adults with impaired fasting glucose and/or impaired glucose tolerance
candidates.measure: Insulin sensitivity and insulin secretion indices from a frequently sampled OGTT (insulin, C-peptide, glucose), plus liver fat by MR spectroscopy
candidates.decision: Offer an intensified rather than conventional lifestyle programme to a high-risk phenotype
candidates.evidence: C073 (PLIS, multicentre RCT, 1105 people, 12 months plus 2-year follow-up): high-risk phenotype defined by secretion, sensitivity and liver fat; randomised high-risk arms to conventional or intensified lifestyle. Excerpt does not show the result for the intensification question.
candidates.guideline_mention: Not found in the screened records.
candidates.why_not_covered: Row 17 and row 45 cover routine HOMA-IR or OGTT indices for prediction. This candidate is a trial-tested treatment-intensity choice based on phenotype, and includes liver fat, which is not an insulin measure.
candidates.first_pass_viability: Likely tier D: it needs a multi-sample OGTT and an MR fat measure, and a single RCT shows phenotype-dependent response only; possible tier C if replicated.
candidates.needed: Replication of the intensification benefit, a simplified phenotype algorithm (fewer samples), and a hard outcome (incident diabetes) rather than post-challenge glucose.

candidates.name: Pre-transplant C-peptide for selecting simultaneous pancreas-kidney transplant recipients (insulin-dependent type 2 phenotype)
candidates.patient_group: Insulin-treated diabetes with kidney failure being considered for pancreas transplant
candidates.measure: Pre-transplant C-peptide (detectable vs undetectable, level around 0.5 and 2.0 ng/mL as reported in C171)
candidates.measure_type: random or fasting C-peptide (measure type not stated in excerpt)
candidates.decision: Whether to list a C-peptide-positive patient for pancreas transplant, and how to counsel on graft risk
candidates.evidence: C171 (matched case-control, 46 vs 46): lower 5-year pancreas graft survival (60% vs 86%) in C-peptide-positive patients, more graft loss from insulin resistance. C166 (retrospective, 214 transplants): outcomes equivalent in carefully selected type 2 phenotype but more pancreatitis and BK virus complications. Results conflict in direction.
candidates.guideline_mention: Not found in the screened records.
candidates.why_not_covered: Row 10 covers C-peptide to classify graft function after transplant (Igls). This is pre-transplant candidate selection and prognosis, a different decision at a different time. C166 and C171 are tied to row 10 only by topic.
candidates.first_pass_viability: Likely tier D: two small retrospective single-centre studies disagree on net benefit.
candidates.needed: A multicentre registry analysis with a defined pre-transplant C-peptide threshold and graft or patient survival outcomes, adjusted for BMI and insulin dose.

candidates.name: OGTT insulin and C-peptide ratios as an outpatient alternative to the 72-hour fast for insulinoma
candidates.patient_group: Adults with suspected insulinoma who cannot easily have an inpatient fast
candidates.measure: Insulin 2 h/0 h ratio and C-peptide 1 h/0 h ratio during a 3-h OGTT
candidates.evidence: C249 (case-control, 37 insulinoma vs 42 controls, one centre): reported AUC 0.97, sensitivity 86.5%, specificity 95.2% for a two-ratio logistic model, no external validation seen. C245 (review) states the 72-h fast is the standardised provocation test.
candidates.guideline_mention: Not found in the screened records; C245 describes the fast as the standard test.
candidates.why_not_covered: Row 23 covers OGTT-induced hypoglycaemia in postprandial insulinoma when a fast is negative, using absolute insulin and glucose. C249 is a derived ratio model used as a first-line outpatient diagnostic replacement, in a case-control (not consecutive-patient) design.
candidates.first_pass_viability: Likely tier D: single small case-control with a self-derived model and no validation; spectrum bias likely.
candidates.needed: Prospective validation in consecutive patients with suspected hypoglycaemia (including reactive and post-bariatric cases) against the 72-h fast, with assay-specific cut-offs.

candidates.name: HOMA-IR criterion in the MAFLD definition for lean or normal-weight adults
candidates.patient_group: Adults with fatty liver who are not overweight
candidates.decision: Whether a lean person with steatosis meets the MAFLD definition
candidates.evidence: C061 (international expert consensus on MAFLD definition): the excerpt did not show a HOMA-IR criterion and my grep of the local text found no 'HOMA' hit, so the use is not confirmed in the corpus. [recall] the 2020 definition lists HOMA-IR 2.5 or higher as one of the metabolic criteria; unverified.
candidates.guideline_mention: Unverified: the consensus may name HOMA-IR; not confirmed in the local text.
candidates.why_not_covered: Row 14 covers HOMA-IR in suspected MASLD (2023 nomenclature, which uses cardiometabolic criteria that do not require an insulin test per C097). The 2020 MAFLD definition is a separate, partly superseded definition.
candidates.first_pass_viability: Likely tier D: superseded definition, unconfirmed in the corpus.
candidates.needed: Read the full MAFLD text for the lean criterion; check whether MASLD (C097) dropped it.

candidates.name: Insulin-resistance index to detect NASH or fibrosis in severe obesity before bariatric surgery; change in HOMA-IR as fibrosis-progression marker in NAFLD
candidates.patient_group: People with severe obesity having bariatric surgery; non-diabetic NAFLD
candidates.measure: HOMA-IR; oral glucose insulin sensitivity index (OGIS, from OGTT); change in HOMA-IR over time
candidates.decision: Flag NASH or fibrosis for biopsy or liver follow-up; monitor fibrosis risk
candidates.evidence: C243 (diagnostic, 90 patients with biopsy): 1/OGIS plus visceral adiposity index separated NASH from simple steatosis (p 0.02), HOMA-IR above 3.5 in moderate or severe steatosis; APRI was the only fibrosis score that rose with significant fibrosis. C075 (cohort, Kangbuk Samsung): changes in an insulin resistance index linked to fibrosis risk (design only from excerpt). C254 (fibrosis score development) has no usable abstract text in the digest.
candidates.guideline_mention: Not found in the screened records for these specific uses (row 14 notes a MASLD guidance table that lists IR tests).
candidates.why_not_covered: Row 14 covers diagnosis of suspected MASLD. These candidates are a pre-surgery NASH triage and a longitudinal prognostic marker, with p-values near 0.02 to 0.05 in small samples.
candidates.first_pass_viability: Likely tier D: small single-centre association with no outcome tied to the decision.
candidates.needed: External validation against biopsy with an incremental-value analysis over FIB-4 or elastography, and a decision threshold.

candidates.name: Metformin for people with bipolar depression who have insulin resistance
candidates.patient_group: Adults with treatment-resistant bipolar depression and insulin resistance
candidates.measure: Insulin resistance by HOMA-style criteria as trial entry and 'converter' status (exact definition not in excerpt)
candidates.decision: Add metformin to reverse insulin resistance and improve depression
candidates.evidence: C079 (TRIO-BD, quadruple-masked RCT, 26 weeks): primary outcome was depression change in those who stopped meeting IR criteria vs those who did not. Result and size not in the excerpt.
candidates.guideline_mention: Not found in the screened records.
candidates.why_not_covered: Row 13 (IRIS) is IR-selected pioglitazone in stroke. No row covers psychiatric selection by IR; rows 43 and 50 cover antipsychotic metabolic monitoring only.
candidates.first_pass_viability: Likely tier D: one trial, a research-defined IR threshold, and a post-randomisation (converter) grouping.
candidates.needed: Trial result with IR as a pre-specified effect modifier, and a replicated threshold.

candidates.name: Baseline insulin or HOMA as predictive biomarker in oncology (metformin in breast cancer; hyperinsulinaemia on PI3K inhibitors)
candidates.patient_group: Women with early breast cancer on adjuvant therapy; patients on PI3K-pathway inhibitors
candidates.measure: Fasting insulin and HOMA; insulin response to the drug
candidates.decision: Choose metformin or add insulin-lowering measures (for example diet or SGLT2 inhibitors [recall]) to improve drug efficacy
candidates.evidence: C170 (MA.32 RCT, full population): metformin vs placebo effect on weight and circulating factors, interaction with baseline BMI and insulin explored (result not in excerpt). C165 (Hopkins, preclinical mouse): hyperinsulinaemia reactivates PI3K signalling and limits efficacy of PI3K inhibitors.
candidates.guideline_mention: Not found in the screened records.
candidates.why_not_covered: Row 40 records alpelisib hyperglycaemia as unsupported, with insulin mentions mechanistic. The metformin-in-breast-cancer biomarker question is not in any row.
candidates.first_pass_viability: Likely tier D (research-only): mouse data and a metabolic-factor analysis with no insulin-guided decision tested.
candidates.needed: A trial that randomises or stratifies by on-treatment insulin level, and clinical outcome (progression), not glucose or insulin change.

candidates.name: Estimated insulin sensitivity in the etiologic classification of youth diabetes
candidates.patient_group: Children and adolescents with newly diagnosed diabetes
candidates.measure: Estimated insulin sensitivity score (clinical equation, not an insulin assay) with islet autoantibodies
candidates.decision: Assign type 1 vs type 2 vs other for treatment
candidates.evidence: C252 (SEARCH, population-based): provider-diagnosed type compared with an etiologic definition based on autoantibodies and estimated insulin sensitivity. Accuracy figures not in the excerpt.
candidates.guideline_mention: Not found in the screened records; the excerpt says the etiologic framework informed international guidelines.
candidates.why_not_covered: Rows 6, 31 and 33 use C-peptide. This is an equation-based sensitivity estimate plus antibodies; it needs no insulin or C-peptide assay.
candidates.first_pass_viability: Likely tier D: surrogate of uncertain value, and it is the reference standard in a registry rather than a clinical test.
candidates.needed: Accuracy of the equation against C-peptide or clamp, and a clinical-pathway test.

refinements.missing_piece: Analogue cross-reactivity of the insulin assay and a worked clinical pitfall
refinements.note: C272 (case) shows factitious hypoglycaemia in an infant missed by a commercial assay that did not detect an insulin analogue. C175 (title only) evaluates which insulin forms two new immunoassays detect. C276 covers factitious hypoglycaemia in insulin-treated diabetes; C264 (retrospective, 70 non-diabetic patients) gives prevalence and characteristics of factitious cases. All fit the path to viability already written for row 2.

refinements.missing_piece: Prevalence of drug-induced factitious hypoglycaemia in non-diabetic patients
refinements.note: C264 is a single-centre retrospective study; it can add the secretagogue share to row 3.

refinements.missing_piece: Numeric C-peptide thresholds from registry data
refinements.note: C271 (CITR, 677 islet-alone recipients): fasting C-peptide and mixed-meal C-peptide-to-glucose ratio predicted insulin independence and HbA1c outcomes; cut points reported 0.33 nmol/L fasting for the optimal outcome and 0.97 nmol/L stimulated. This is the numeric, validated-against-outcome piece row 10 lists as missing. C253 (retrospective) tests modified Igls in islet autograft after total pancreatectomy, also relevant to row 27.

refinements.missing_piece: Glucose-based substitute for HOMA-IR selection, and heart-failure safety in IR patients
refinements.note: C055 says IR is not commonly measured in practice and reports pioglitazone benefit in IRIS participants defined by prediabetes (HbA1c or fasting glucose), a route that avoids insulin testing. C164 (IRIS post hoc) addresses heart failure risk, relevant to the benefit-harm balance of treating IR-selected patients.

refinements.missing_piece: Monitoring of type B insulin resistance by fasting insulin
refinements.note: C275 (patients at NIH, longitudinal): receptor-antibody titre correlated with fasting insulin (rho 0.825 per grep of text); severe disease was defined with fasting insulin above 100 uU/mL. C251 (systematic review) names high fasting insulin with high adiponectin and normal or low triglycerides as a diagnostic clue, and insulin doses above 3 U/kg/day as a trigger for testing. These add a monitoring and referral-trigger use to row 12.

refinements.missing_piece: Comparator performance of the mixed-meal test vs CGM
refinements.note: C260 (15 post-bypass patients, 8 asymptomatic, 9 controls): mixed-meal test sensitivity 71% vs CGM 47%, specificity 100% vs 88%, on glucose; the abstract excerpt does not say insulin was part of the test. It gives row 5 a glucose-based accuracy figure but does not show that insulin adds value.

refinements.missing_piece: Emergency-department and neonatal settings for the critical sample
refinements.note: C232 (retrospective, children in an ED) evaluated hypoglycaemia during a spontaneous event or a fasting study with insulin and counter-regulatory hormones measured. C236 found hyperinsulinism in 52 of 58 infants with persistent neonatal hypoglycaemia after the 2015 guideline. Both support the row 4 critical-sample use in practice settings.

refinements.missing_piece: Pooled diagnostic accuracy of arterial stimulation venous sampling
refinements.note: C242 (systematic review and meta-analysis) covers ASVS accuracy for localisation (numbers not in the excerpt). C237 (80 operated insulinoma patients), C245 (review, imaging may replace sampling) and C255 (case, 68Ga-exendin PET) show imaging competing with insulin-gradient sampling, which weakens the case for row 22.

refinements.missing_piece: Pre-test probability model to decide who needs C-peptide testing
refinements.note: C239 and C250 (clinical model validated with C-peptide-defined insulin deficiency and histology) and C268 (10 published approaches compared against C-peptide at more than 3 years) use C-peptide as a reference standard. They support triage rules for who should receive random C-peptide (rows 6 and 31). C278 (editorial) says up to 40% of adults over 30 with type 1 may be misdiagnosed [stated in excerpt as an estimate].

refinements.missing_piece: C-peptide inclusion criterion in youth monogenic-diabetes screening
refinements.note: C256 (ProDiGY) used antibody-negative status and fasting C-peptide above 0.6 ng/mL as part of enrolment for youth with presumed type 2 diabetes. C241 (Swedish national cohort) argues that absent antibodies plus modestly raised glucose should lead to MODY testing. Both give a C-peptide-based screening rule for row 7 in a US youth population.

refinements.missing_piece: Population reference intervals and non-linear risk by glucose-tolerance status
refinements.note: C071 (title only) proposes HOMA-IR reference intervals. C085 (prospective cohort): the HOMA-IR to cardiovascular risk link varies by glucose tolerance. C088 (meta-analysis, 38 studies) gives HRs for diabetes and non-fatal MACE. C062 (Mendelian randomisation) supports causality. C076 and C053 show that surrogate indices have limited reproducibility and that correlation with the clamp is not enough. None gives a decision rule, so row 17 stays unsupported.

refinements.missing_piece: Assay harmonisation and pre-analytical stability for insulin and C-peptide
refinements.note: Seven papers show assay discordance, new platforms, an isotope-dilution mass spectrometry reference method and sample-stability limits. They are the standardisation piece the path-to-viability text for rows 1, 2, 6, 7 and 10 already requests.

refinements.missing_piece: More trials using C-peptide as the endpoint
refinements.note: C247 (CLOuD protocol, closed-loop insulin in new-onset youth, residual beta-cell function as outcome) and C060 (albiglutide) add endpoint citations; research-only status unchanged.

notes: Scanned the whole digest (112 entries). 39 carry an existing row tie; 73 do not. Of the 73, about 20 are epidemiology, case reports or background guidelines with no insulin or C-peptide decision (C230, C231, C233, C234, C246, C274, C279, C172, C270, C174, C167, C168, C265, C267, C257, C266, C248 and others). C248, C257 and C266 duplicate rows 20 and 21. Only abstract excerpts were available for most entries, so strengths are abstract-level; two entries had no local text (C071, C093, C175, C277 are title only). One grep on local full texts (C101, C061, C073, C256, C079, C170, C275) was used for specific passages. C061 HOMA-IR criterion was not found in the local text and is flagged unverified. No web use.
